facts.label: Financial foundation analysis
facts.text: Reported leverage rose while adjusted leverage fell. Net debt over trailing reported EBITDA moved from 2.21x at fiscal year-end 2025 to 2.35x at 2026-10-02, whereas net debt over the issuer's adjusted measure moved from 2.17x to 2.07x. The divergence sits in the denominator: nine-month spin-off costs of USD 70 million, against USD 4 million a year earlier, reduce reported EBITDA, and the issuer adds back USD 72 million of spin-off, acquisition and restructuring costs together with a new add-back of USD 44 million for its share of joint venture interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation. For creditors the reported series is the like-for-like one, because the new add-back was applied from 2026 without restating earlier periods. Basis: calculation K4; calculation K8; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_q326kbr-exhibit991x10022026.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 4

facts.label: Financial foundation analysis
facts.text: Cash flow quality weakened even though net debt held. Operating cash flow from continuing operations fell to USD 331 million in the nine months to 2026-10-02 from USD 506 million a year earlier, because receivables absorbed USD 218 million against USD 40 million while payables and customer advances added USD 134 million and USD 99 million. The inflow from customer advances is a non-debt funding float: contract liabilities rose to USD 429 million from USD 331 million at fiscal year-end, and the company says it often receives cash in advance on sustainable technology projects, so the balance unwinds as that work is delivered and the inflow would reverse. Spin-off transaction costs paid of USD 40 million sit inside the USD 331 million, which the issuer adjusts to USD 371 million. Basis: calculation K9; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, pages 4–7; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 48; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_q326kbr-exhibit991x10022026.htm.jsonl, page 15

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case against caution is that the spin-off is built to cut debt and the business that keeps the name has the faster-growing order book: backlog covers 2.27x trailing revenue, Sustainable Technology Solutions backlog rose 35.2%, the issuer reports net leverage of 2.1x, and KBR intends to apply the cash distribution to reduce indebtedness. facts.label: Company description and business model
facts.text: KBR, Inc. is a Delaware corporation headquartered in Houston that sells engineering, technology and logistics services through two segments. Mission Technology Solutions serves defence, intelligence, space and aviation programmes, mainly for U.S., U.K. and Australian agencies, and includes the Aspire Defence concession, a 35-year U.K. contract whose publicly held bonds are non-recourse to KBR. Sustainable Technology Solutions licenses more than 85 proprietary process technologies in ammonia, chemicals, refining and circular-economy processes and adds engineering, advisory and digital services for commercial and international government clients. Revenue was USD 7,786 million in fiscal 2025, up 1.0% after 10.8% in fiscal 2024, the year of the LinQuest acquisition, and USD 5,935 million in the nine months to 2026-10-02, up 0.6%. facts.label: Ownership and group structure
facts.text: KBR is a widely held public company: 52 shareholders of record are reported, no controlling holder or sponsor is named in the filings read, and board composition, beneficial ownership and executive pay sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied. KBR, Inc. is the borrower under the Senior Credit Facility and the issuer of the Senior Notes, and its domestic subsidiaries guarantee both. Joint ventures sit outside the borrower group, with Aspire Defence at 45%, Affinity at 50%, Brown & Root Industrial Services at 50%, the Ichthys venture at 30% and the Plaquemines venture at 45%, so project lenders rank ahead of KBR's equity interests at joint venture level and KBR carries joint and several performance exposure with no stated cap. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Pricing power is limited by the contract form rather than by market position. In Mission Technology Solutions the price is allowable cost plus fee under federal rules, procurement practice sometimes emphasises price over technical merit, and many contracts are recompeted, so margin comes from mix and execution. In Sustainable Technology Solutions the company says its technology portfolio enhances margins and attributes the fall in operating income to licensing mix, so a shift toward engineering and professional services is the likely reason revenue rose 11.1% while operating income fell 8%. The split of revenue between licensing and services is not printed, so pricing power on licences is not testable. Basis: calculation F6; calculation F17; 10-K_2026-01-02_kbr-20260102.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; 10-K_2026-01-02_kbr-20260102.htm.jsonl, pages 53–55; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 44

facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Margins can be defended under volume pressure where costs are reimbursable, since allowable costs and a fee are recovered, but not under cost inflation on fixed-price work, where the company says technical problems, schedule delays, workforce issues, material availability and inflation can raise costs to complete and reduce profit. Group margin stability is masked by segment movement: Mission Technology Solutions gross margin rose to 13.9% from 12.4% while Sustainable Technology Solutions fell to 15.6% from 19.2%. facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Competitive rivalry is intense in federal services: contracts are awarded competitively, often under multiple-award vehicles, and recompetes let rivals take share, with larger competitors holding more resources, so margin on new awards can be pressed. Barriers to entry are real but not decisive: cleared staff, facility clearances and past performance protect incumbency, yet award protests can delay revenue and cash. The credit effect is limited share loss at the margin rather than a sudden step-down. facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Substitutes matter in two places: government agencies can insource work, as the NASA insourcing debooking shows and as the company says it competes with the government's own capabilities, and rapid technology change could erode the edge of licensed processes. Buyer power is high because the U.S. government is 57% of revenue, can modify or terminate contracts for convenience and reviews costs for allowability, and commercial energy customers defer projects when commodity prices move. Supplier power is modest, since equipment and materials come from a variety of global sources, but letters of credit and surety capacity beyond the revolver are at providers' discretion, which makes banks the supplier that matters to awards. facts.label: Political, regulatory and economic factors
facts.text: Political and regulatory factors are material to credit. The fiscal 2027 federal budget is not enacted, the continuing resolution lapses on 2026-12-11, an April 2026 executive order directs reviews of private-sector contracts, federal staff reductions may delay awards, and procurement reform may raise competition and compliance burdens; against this, defence appropriations of USD 839 billion for fiscal 2026 and NATO and Australian spending commitments support demand. For creditors the effect is timing risk to Mission Technology Solutions awards and cash, not a demonstrated loss of revenue. facts.label: Financial profile and credit quality
facts.text: Scale is adequate and breadth is moderate: trailing revenue of USD 7,820 million comes from two segments, U.S. and U.K. government customers are 66% of fiscal 2025 revenue, and the business that stays is smaller, less diversified and more exposed to the Middle East. Cost and capex flexibility is good because capital spending is 0.61% of revenue and 38.2% of revenue is cost-reimbursable. Margin stability is average at group level, with gross margin at 14.5% against 14.6%, and weaker in the business that stays, where gross margin fell to 15.6% from 19.2%. Free cash flow is lower and more discretionary than a year ago, at USD 295 million against USD 482 million. The ability to refinance cannot be tested against ratings or prices because none are supplied; the only market evidence is fair values at 97.2% of principal for the Senior Notes and 100.2% for Term Loan B. Liquidity is adequate at 1.89x current maturities, and financial policy is restrained but undocumented. The trend is flat leverage on lower cash generation, and the missing data that matter are the separation financing, covenant ratios and definitions, and corporate cost allocation. facts.label: Qualitative downside scenario
facts.text: The scenario begins with the separation financing, because it is the one event that moves leverage without any change in operations. If the spun business's financing yields a distribution of only 1.0x its annualised Adjusted EBITDA, USD 588 million, net debt after the distribution would be USD 1,514 million against annualised Adjusted EBITDA of USD 448 million for the business that stays, or 3.38x. facts.label: Qualitative downside scenario
facts.text: The first operational break would be a stall in Sustainable Technology Solutions earnings, already down 6.5% without the new add-back, together with weaker cash conversion if customer advances unwind below the USD 331 million of fiscal 2025. The financial transmission is higher leverage on lower EBITDA, a step-up in interest as swaps with USD 955 million of notional end by January 2027, and a refinancing of Term Loan A-2 in August 2027 negotiated at a higher leverage. Liquidity would hold, since cash and undrawn revolver of USD 1,046 million cover USD 554 million of current maturities 1.89x, so the pressure is on leverage, pricing and covenant room rather than on liquidity distress. Management levers are USD 63 million of dividends, USD 29 million of repurchases, USD 189 million of discretionary investments and USD 36 million of capital spending. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through 2027 but not to preserve the current 2.07x. Basis: calculation F5; calculation F8; calculation F10; calculation F12; calculation F14; calculation F16; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, pages 28–29

facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, KBR presents an adequate business profile supported by low capital intensity, a cost-reimbursable government core, covered near-term maturities and a visible order book, but credit quality is constrained by an unquantified separation financing that will move debt onto a business holding 43.2% of nine-month Adjusted EBITDA, by earnings quality that leans on LNG estimate changes and joint venture equity earnings, and by margin dilution at the business that stays. Cash-flow durability appears adequate due to low capital spending, cost pass-through and USD 515 million of fiscal 2025 free cash flow, but it is lower and more discretionary in 2026. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the size of the separation distribution, the extension of Term Loan A-2, the fate of the swaps and market access that no rating or price evidences. The primary downside path is a small distribution followed by a funding delay and a fade in LNG benefits. Further analysis would require the Form 10 financing and debt allocation, the covenant definitions and ratios, corporate cost allocation, and the executed credit agreement. Top risk: remaining-group leverage after separation. Basis: calculation F1; calculation F7; calculation F8; calculation F9; calculation F13; Source readiness (CP-0); Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

## Findings
### Bottom line

The supplied filings support a credit snapshot of KBR as of 2026-11-05 only for the group before the planned January 2027 spin-off of Mission Technology Solutions, so creditors cannot yet see the debt each company will carry.

The filings say only that the business being spun off will pay KBR a cash distribution from its own financing, to be used to reduce debt, and the amount and the debt each company keeps are not established.

For the existing group, the latest quarterly report was published 7 days before the as-of date, and total debt of USD 2,541 million and the covenant levels are stated in the notes. No credit agreement, indenture, rating, market price, separation registration statement or proxy statement is supplied, so covenant headroom, tranche-level maturities and post-separation leverage are not established.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Net leverage is moderate but depends on the EBITDA definition: net debt is 2.35x trailing reported EBITDA at 2026-10-02 against 2.07x on the issuer's adjusted measure, so the two series now point in opposite directions.
Net debt itself barely moved, USD 2,102 million against USD 2,096 million at fiscal year-end 2025, and no separation financing is yet quantified, so no pro forma figure is stated.
Basis: calculation K3; calculation K4; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_q326kbr-exhibit991x10022026.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 52

Debt of USD 2,541 million at carrying value includes USD 554 million due within 12 months, which cash and undrawn revolver of USD 1,046 million cover 1.89 times. Interest cover was 6.72x in fiscal 2025 on cash interest paid, but the quarterly reports print no cash interest, so cover at 2026-10-02 is not calculable.
Basis: calculation K3; calculation K4; calculation K5; calculation K7; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 20
### Financial foundation analysis

Reported leverage rose while adjusted leverage fell. Net debt over trailing reported EBITDA moved from 2.21x at fiscal year-end 2025 to 2.35x at 2026-10-02, whereas net debt over the issuer's adjusted measure moved from 2.17x to 2.07x. The divergence sits in the denominator: nine-month spin-off costs of USD 70 million, against USD 4 million a year earlier, reduce reported EBITDA, and the issuer adds back USD 72 million of spin-off, acquisition and restructuring costs together with a new add-back of USD 44 million for its share of joint venture interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation. For creditors the reported series is the like-for-like one, because the new add-back was applied from 2026 without restating earlier periods.
Basis: calculation K4; calculation K8; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_q326kbr-exhibit991x10022026.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 4

Cash flow quality weakened even though net debt held. Operating cash flow from continuing operations fell to USD 331 million in the nine months to 2026-10-02 from USD 506 million a year earlier, because receivables absorbed USD 218 million against USD 40 million while payables and customer advances added USD 134 million and USD 99 million. The inflow from customer advances is a non-debt funding float: contract liabilities rose to USD 429 million from USD 331 million at fiscal year-end, and the company says it often receives cash in advance on sustainable technology projects, so the balance unwinds as that work is delivered and the inflow would reverse. Spin-off transaction costs paid of USD 40 million sit inside the USD 331 million, which the issuer adjusts to USD 371 million.
Basis: calculation K9; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, pages 4–7; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 48; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_q326kbr-exhibit991x10022026.htm.jsonl, page 15

Interest cover is only measurable on an annual basis. Reported EBITDA of USD 947 million covered cash interest paid of USD 141 million 6.72x in fiscal 2025, up from 6.57x in fiscal 2024, while the income-statement proxy gives 6.17x on the trailing twelve months to 2026-10-02, using interest expense of USD 145 million. The quarterly reports do not print cash interest paid, so the trailing cash measure cannot be built and the proxy is labelled as such.
Basis: calculation K4; calculation K6; 10-K_2026-01-02_kbr-20260102.htm.jsonl, page 116; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 7

Liquidity and maturities need the revolver, not cash alone. At 2026-10-02 cash of USD 439 million plus undrawn revolver of USD 607 million after USD 18 million of letters of credit gives USD 1,046 million, against USD 554 million of current maturities that include the Term Loan A-2 due August 2027; the issuer's USD 625 million of revolver capacity equals the commitment less borrowings and so does not deduct those letters of credit. The maturity table at fiscal year-end 2025 shows USD 551 million due in fiscal 2027, USD 285 million in fiscal 2028 and USD 788 million in fiscal 2029, so refinancing is concentrated in the next three years. A schedule at 2026-10-02 is not printed.
Basis: calculation K5; calculation K7; 10-K_2026-01-02_kbr-20260102.htm.jsonl, page 97; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, pages 17–20

Data quality and definitions limit comparisons. Every statement identity holds at each date, but the annual report prints no EBITDA, the segment tables changed basis in 2026, the quarterly reports omit cash interest, and issuer net debt of USD 2,118 million uses principal while this module's net debt of USD 2,102 million uses carrying value. The planned cash distribution from the business to be spun off, which KBR intends to use to cut debt, is not quantified, so net debt stays the pre-separation figure.
Basis: calculation K3; calculation K1; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 52; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_q326kbr-exhibit991x10022026.htm.jsonl, page 2

- Severity High. The separation financing is not quantified: the cash distribution that the business to be spun off will pay KBR to reduce debt has no stated amount, instrument or date, and the registration statement on Form 10 is not supplied, so post-separation net debt and leverage are not established; this restricts every forward view of leverage until the document is supplied.

- Severity Medium. Cash interest paid is not printed in the quarterly reports for the nine months to 2026-10-02 and 2025-10-03, so trailing interest cover on cash interest is not calculable; the income-statement proxy is shown instead; supply the cash flow supplemental disclosure.

- Severity Medium. The maturity ladder is drawn at fiscal year-end 2025 only. Source readiness states that no schedule of maturities by year is printed; the annual report prints one in its contractual obligations table, which this module uses, so that statement is corrected here for 2026-01-02 only. No schedule is printed at 2026-10-02, so the 2026 repayments are not reflected; supply an updated ladder.

- Severity Medium. Term Loan A principal is reported as one line across three tranches in two currencies, so the amount maturing in August 2027 is not printed; this limits the refinancing view to dated maturities; supply the tranche schedule.

## Findings
### Bottom line

KBR is a government-weighted services group whose creditor perimeter is about to shrink: the Mission Technology Solutions business to be spun off supplied 65.2% of nine-month revenue and 56.8% of Adjusted EBITDA, so creditors depend on a debt reduction that is not yet quantified.

The remaining group, Sustainable Technology Solutions plus corporate costs, would carry USD 336 million of nine-month Adjusted EBITDA if corporate costs stayed in full, 43.2% of the consolidated figure.
Basis: calculation M1; calculation M3; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 52

Operations are steady rather than strained: U.S. government customers were 57% of fiscal 2025 revenue, backlog is USD 17,718 million, and no sponsor or extraction behaviour is documented. Governance detail for creditors is thin because board and ownership information sits in a proxy statement that is not supplied.
### Key findings

- Government demand is the anchor and the main exposure. U.S. government customers produced 57% of fiscal 2025 revenue and U.K. government customers 9%, and cost-reimbursable work was 38.2% of nine-month revenue in 2026, which passes cost overruns to customers but ties revenue to appropriations; a continuing resolution funds the U.S. government only through 2026-12-11 and no fiscal 2027 budget is enacted, so award timing is the near-term risk.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-02_kbr-20260102.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation M6

- The two segments are diverging, and the faster-growing one is the one that stays. Mission Technology Solutions revenue fell 4.3% in the nine months on lower NASA-related programme revenue and lower European command activity, while Sustainable Technology Solutions revenue rose 11.1% and its backlog rose 35.2% to USD 5,828 million, although its operating income fell 8% on licensing mix.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 46; calculation M7

- The spin-off, not operations, is the main credit event. The business to be spun off supplied 65.2% of revenue and 56.8% of Adjusted EBITDA, segment-level corporate costs of USD 71 million sit with neither segment today, and the filings say only that it will pay KBR a cash distribution from its own financing to reduce debt; the amount, the instruments and the debt each company keeps are not stated, so the remaining group's leverage cannot be measured.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 52; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_q326kbr-exhibit991x10022026.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation M1; calculation M3

- Shareholder returns are material but have been funded from operating cash flow, and the sources name no sponsor or controlling holder. Repurchases and dividends took 74.1% of fiscal 2025 operating cash flow from continuing operations and 27.8% in the nine months to 2026-10-02, as repurchases fell to USD 29 million with USD 402 million of authorisation remaining.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-02_kbr-20260102.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 58; calculation M8

- Joint ventures and performance guarantees create exposure outside reported debt. Equity in earnings of unconsolidated affiliates was 31.0% of nine-month operating income, services to joint ventures were USD 710 million of fiscal 2025 revenue, joint venture partners are usually jointly and severally liable for performance guarantees with no maximum estimable, and a USD 41 million Kuwait court judgment against KBR is unaccrued and under appeal; the Aspire Defence bonds are non-recourse to KBR.
Basis: 10-K_2026-01-02_kbr-20260102.htm.jsonl, page 148; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 54; calculation M10; calculation M12

- Disclosure is adequate for performance but thin for governance. Internal control over financial reporting was audited as effective at fiscal year-end 2025 and the auditor has served since 2005, but board composition, ownership and pay sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied, 52 shareholders of record are reported, and a multi-phase systems implementation is altering controls.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against caution is that the spin-off is built to cut debt and the business that keeps the name has the faster-growing order book: backlog covers 2.27x trailing revenue, Sustainable Technology Solutions backlog rose 35.2%, the issuer reports net leverage of 2.1x, and KBR intends to apply the cash distribution to reduce indebtedness. The view would turn constructive if the registration statement shows separation financing large enough to retire debt in line with the 56.8% of Adjusted EBITDA that leaves, and it would worsen if the distribution is small, because the remaining group would then carry most of the existing debt on 43.2% of earnings at best. A lapse in U.S. government funding after 2026-12-11 or a further decline in NASA-related work would weaken the Mission Technology Solutions earnings that support the spin-off financing.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 46; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_q326kbr-exhibit991x10022026.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation M1; calculation M3; calculation M9
### Limitations

- The registration statement on Form 10 and the proxy statement are not supplied, so the post-separation debt allocation, the governance of both companies and ownership detail are not established, which limits the perimeter conclusion to the pre-separation group.

- Beneficial ownership is not stated in the sources, so the absence of a controlling holder rests on the filings naming none and on 52 holders of record, and it would change if a large holder were disclosed.

- Segment results sit on two bases, the fiscal 2025 alignment in the annual report and the 2026 alignment with recast comparatives, so the segment-mix conclusions use only the nine-month 2026 and 2025 figures.
- Backlog is the issuer's own measure and includes its share of unconsolidated joint ventures, so the coverage figure overstates consolidated revenue visibility.
- No investor presentation is supplied, so the strategy language comes from filings and releases and is treated as management language.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

No new notes or term loans were issued in 2026 in the sources read; the only change to the debt documents was Credit Agreement Amendment No. 14 on 2026-07-29, which permits the internal reorganisation needed for the spin-off, and the Senior Notes remain USD 250 million due in 2028. The spin-off of the Mission Technology Solutions business is targeted for 2027-01-04 and is conditional on Board approval, a tax opinion or ruling, effectiveness of the Form 10 and satisfactory completion of financing, and the business is to pay KBR a cash distribution from its own financing before completion, which KBR intends to use to reduce debt; no amount is stated.

# KBR, INC. - Fundamental credit as of 2026-11-05
## Request

KBR, INC. (issuer id kbr), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the integrated fundamental credit view of the consolidated group before the planned January 2027 spin-off of Mission Technology Solutions: business risk, financial profile, downside path and monitoring triggers.

## Findings
### Bottom line

KBR is an adequate credit before separation, with moderate leverage and little capital intensity, but creditors' position after the planned January 2027 spin-off of Mission Technology Solutions depends on a debt reduction that the filings do not quantify. Net debt is USD 2,102 million, 2.35x trailing reported EBITDA and 2.07x on the issuer's adjusted measure; no pro forma figure for the planned cash distribution is established. Excluding the add-back introduced in 2026, adjusted leverage is 2.16x against 2.17x at fiscal 2025 year-end, so it has barely moved. The business that stays, after all corporate costs, supplied 43.2% of nine-month Adjusted EBITDA, so on an illustrative basis its leverage would be 4.69x without a distribution.
Basis: calculation F1; calculation F2; calculation F4; calculation F7; calculation F8; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 52; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Key findings

- The spin-off is the credit event, and its financing is the unknown. Mission Technology Solutions supplied 65.2% of nine-month revenue and 56.8% of Adjusted EBITDA, while the filings say only that it will pay KBR a cash distribution from its own financing to reduce debt, and they list the spun company's ability to borrow enough for that distribution as a risk. If the remaining business, with annualised nine-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 448 million after all corporate costs, kept today's net debt, leverage would be 4.69x. A distribution of about USD 1,175 million, 2.00x the spun business's annualised Adjusted EBITDA, would hold today's 2.07x, while a distribution of only 1.0x would leave 3.38x. These are illustrations, not forecasts.

Basis: calculation F7; calculation F8; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-K_2026-01-02_kbr-20260102.htm.jsonl, page 51; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_q326kbr-exhibit991x10022026.htm.jsonl, page 14

- Leverage is moderate and flat like-for-like. Net debt over trailing reported EBITDA is 2.35x against 2.21x at fiscal 2025 year-end because nine-month reported EBITDA fell USD 52 million after USD 70 million of spin-off costs and other charges, and the issuer's improvement in adjusted leverage from 2.17x to 2.07x becomes 2.16x once the USD 44 million add-back introduced in 2026 is removed. Net debt moved only from USD 2,096 million to USD 2,102 million, income-statement interest cover is 6.17x, and no pro forma figure for the planned cash distribution is established.
Basis: calculation F1; calculation F2; calculation F3; calculation F4; calculation F22; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_q326kbr-exhibit991x10022026.htm.jsonl, page 14; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Cash generation weakened and is being reinvested in affiliates rather than in debt reduction. Free cash flow was USD 295 million in nine months against USD 482 million, or 44.4% of reported EBITDA against 67.3%. The filing attributes the fall primarily to a change order for USD 128 million resolved in the earlier period that did not recur, but USD 189 million went to joint ventures and other investments, including USD 115 million into one joint venture, and dividends and repurchases took USD 92 million, so net debt did not fall. Contract liabilities rose USD 98 million to USD 429 million, a customer-advance float that reverses as work is delivered.

Basis: calculation F9; calculation F10; calculation F11; calculation F12; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 50

- Earnings quality is weaker than the headline, and the business that stays earns less on each dollar of revenue. Favourable estimate changes on one LNG project contributed USD 117 million, 21.7% of nine-month operating income, and if such changes did not recur trailing reported EBITDA would be USD 751 million and net leverage 2.80x. Sustainable Technology Solutions grew revenue 11.1%, but without the new add-back its Adjusted EBITDA fell 6.5% and its margin fell from 21.4% to 18.0%, its gross margin fell from 19.2% to 15.6%, and equity earnings are 38.2% of its operating income.

Basis: calculation F5; calculation F6; calculation F13; calculation F17; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 44

- Government demand is the anchor and the nearest exposure. U.S. government customers were 57% of fiscal 2025 revenue, a continuing resolution funds the government only to 2026-12-11 and no fiscal 2027 budget is enacted. Mission Technology Solutions revenue fell 4.3% in nine months on NASA-related reductions, with federal civilian revenue down 12.4%, and its backlog fell 5.3% since fiscal year-end; fixed-price work rose to 31.9% of revenue from 26.4%, which raises overrun risk. Backlog of USD 17,718 million, 2.27x trailing revenue, and cost-reimbursable work at 38.2% of revenue limit the damage.

Basis: calculation F17; calculation F18; calculation F19; 10-K_2026-01-02_kbr-20260102.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 46

- Near-term liquidity is adequate, but refinancing around the separation is the binding risk. Cash plus undrawn revolver of USD 1,046 million covers current maturities of USD 554 million 1.89x, and 1.75x if USD 77 million of cash held in joint ventures, the Aspire Defence project and a captive insurer is excluded; no pro forma figure for the planned cash distribution is established. Term Loan A-2 falls due in August 2027, 62.1% of principal at fiscal 2025 year-end matures in fiscal 2027 to 2029, 90.2% of principal floats, and swaps with USD 955 million of notional end by January 2027, when the spin-off is targeted. The covenant tests of 4.00x maximum net leverage and 3.00x minimum interest coverage are stated as met, but the ratios are not printed, so headroom is not calculable.

Basis: calculation F14; calculation F15; calculation F16; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, pages 17–20; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, pages 28–29; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-K_2026-01-02_kbr-20260102.htm.jsonl, page 97

- Claims outside reported debt are contained except for joint venture guarantees, which have no cap. Joint venture partners are usually jointly and severally liable for performance guarantees with no maximum estimable, letters of credit outstanding are USD 323 million of which USD 99 million support joint ventures, and capacity beyond the revolver rests with the banks' discretion. A USD 41 million Kuwait judgment is unaccrued and under appeal, receivables sold in nine months were USD 935 million with USD 65 million outstanding, and the U.K. pension is in a USD 120 million surplus.

- Financial policy looks restrained for now but is untested by the spin-off. No sponsor or controlling holder is named, repurchases fell to USD 29 million in nine months from USD 304 million, and returns took 27.8% of operating cash flow against 72.5%, yet USD 402 million of repurchase authorisation remains and credit agreement restrictions, board composition and beneficial ownership are not supplied.
Basis: calculation F23; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26; 10-K_2026-01-02_kbr-20260102.htm.jsonl, page 80; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against caution is that the separation is built to cut debt and the arithmetic is not demanding: holding today's 2.07x needs a distribution of about USD 1,175 million, only 2.00x the spun business's annualised Adjusted EBITDA before any corporate costs it takes over, lenders consented to the reorganisation steps in Amendment No. 14, and KBR states it intends to use the distribution to reduce debt. The business that stays holds a record backlog of USD 5,828 million, up 35.2%, with book-to-bill of 1.3x. Part of the 2026 cash flow fall is a high 2025 comparison, because without the USD 128 million change order the earlier nine months would be USD 378 million against USD 371 million adjusted in 2026. Nine-month capital spending is 0.61% of revenue, and management reaffirmed fiscal 2026 guidance at each quarterly release, with adjusted operating cash flow of USD 560 million to USD 600 million implying USD 189 million to USD 229 million in the fourth quarter.

Basis: calculation F8; calculation F9; calculation F11; calculation F17; calculation F19; calculation F20; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 52; EX-99.1_2026-05-05_q126kbr-exhibit991x04032026.htm.jsonl, page 5; EX-99.1_2026-07-30_q226kbr-exhibit991x07032026.htm.jsonl, page 6; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_q326kbr-exhibit991x10022026.htm.jsonl, pages 3–6

The view would turn constructive if the registration statement shows a distribution near or above USD 1,175 million, Term Loan A-2 is extended or replaced before the spin-off, and fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA is at or above the USD 203 million implied by the guidance floor. It would worsen if the distribution is closer to USD 588 million, which leaves 3.38x, if a lapse in funding after 2026-12-11 delays Mission Technology Solutions awards, or if favourable LNG estimate changes stop while the margin of the business that stays keeps shrinking.
Basis: calculation F8; calculation F13; calculation F20; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 37; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_q326kbr-exhibit991x10022026.htm.jsonl, page 6
### Limitations

- The illustrations of the business that stays use annualised nine-month Adjusted EBITDA, keep all corporate costs with it and leave all existing debt with it, so they size the distribution needed but cannot say where debt will sit; a different allocation in the registration statement would change both the 4.69x and the USD 1,175 million.

- Covenant headroom is not calculable because the covenant definitions and ratios are not printed, so the liquidity conclusion rests on facility availability and the issuer's statement of compliance, and a tighter definition would lower it.

- The LNG project is not named and how much estimate-change benefit remains is not stated, so the earnings-quality conclusion and the 2.80x sensitivity are directional; the benefit could end sooner or later than assumed.

- Pricing power cannot be tested because rate cards, win rates and contract-level margins are not printed, so the view that margins rest on cost-reimbursable terms and mix rather than on pricing is inferred from contract mix alone.

- No ratings, market prices or peer data are supplied, so access to capital markets and competitive standing are judged from the issuer's filings and fair-value notes, and the refinancing conclusion would change with a price for the notes or a rating action.

- The outlook rests on guidance for the whole group before separation, which management says it will replace with separate outlooks, so the fourth-quarter ranges implied by guidance test the current perimeter only.
### Strengths and weaknesses

KBR's credit rests on a capital-light, government-weighted services and technology group whose debt is moderate for its earnings today and whose future depends on how the separation allocates debt and earnings between two companies.
Basis: calculation F1; calculation F7; calculation F9; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 33

Low capital intensity and a cost-reimbursable core are the first strength. Capital spending was USD 36 million in nine months, 0.61% of revenue, and cost-reimbursable work was 38.2% of revenue, so a large part of costs passes to customers and capital spending can flex; this converted fiscal 2025 EBITDA into USD 515 million of free cash flow and supports cash interest cover of 6.72x.
Basis: calculation F9; calculation F18; calculation F22; 10-K_2026-01-02_kbr-20260102.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20; 10-K_2026-01-02_kbr-20260102.htm.jsonl, pages 115–116

Moderate leverage with covered near-term maturities is the second strength. Net leverage is 2.35x on reported EBITDA and 2.07x on the issuer's adjusted measure, and no pro forma figure for the planned cash distribution is established. The issuer states compliance with its covenants, and cash plus undrawn revolver covers current maturities 1.89x, so a delayed refinancing would not by itself create a liquidity shortfall.
Basis: calculation F1; calculation F14; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 20

A visible order book is the third strength. Backlog of USD 17,718 million is 2.27x trailing revenue and the business that stays has a record USD 5,828 million, up 35.2%, so backlog expected to convert to revenue within a year is about 69.7% of trailing revenue, though backlog includes joint venture shares and customers can terminate for convenience.
Basis: calculation F17; calculation F19; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_q326kbr-exhibit991x10022026.htm.jsonl, page 5

The absence of a sponsor and a sharp cut in repurchases are the fourth strength. No controlling holder is named, repurchases fell to USD 29 million from USD 304 million, and operating cash flow covered dividends and repurchases 3.6 times, so there is no documented extraction; the restraint is untested by the separation.

### Company description and business model

KBR, Inc. is a Delaware corporation headquartered in Houston that sells engineering, technology and logistics services through two segments. Mission Technology Solutions serves defence, intelligence, space and aviation programmes, mainly for U.S., U.K. and Australian agencies, and includes the Aspire Defence concession, a 35-year U.K. contract whose publicly held bonds are non-recourse to KBR. Sustainable Technology Solutions licenses more than 85 proprietary process technologies in ammonia, chemicals, refining and circular-economy processes and adds engineering, advisory and digital services for commercial and international government clients. Revenue was USD 7,786 million in fiscal 2025, up 1.0% after 10.8% in fiscal 2024, the year of the LinQuest acquisition, and USD 5,935 million in the nine months to 2026-10-02, up 0.6%.

For creditors, cost-reimbursable government work gives multi-year, cost-protected cash flows, with 36% of USD 13.6 billion of remaining performance obligations due within a year and 41% in years two to five, while technology licensing and engineering are project-based and lumpier. The model is capital-light and working-capital heavy: receivables were USD 1,300 million against customer advances of USD 429 million, so liquidity depends on collections and advances more than on capital spending. Debt service capacity is good at the current perimeter, and refinancing confidence depends on the group staying whole through the separation.

### Ownership and group structure

KBR is a widely held public company: 52 shareholders of record are reported, no controlling holder or sponsor is named in the filings read, and board composition, beneficial ownership and executive pay sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied. KBR, Inc. is the borrower under the Senior Credit Facility and the issuer of the Senior Notes, and its domestic subsidiaries guarantee both. Joint ventures sit outside the borrower group, with Aspire Defence at 45%, Affinity at 50%, Brown & Root Industrial Services at 50%, the Ichthys venture at 30% and the Plaquemines venture at 45%, so project lenders rank ahead of KBR's equity interests at joint venture level and KBR carries joint and several performance exposure with no stated cap.

### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is government-funded and multi-year in Mission Technology Solutions and project-based in Sustainable Technology Solutions. In the nine months, defence and intelligence customers contributed USD 2,486 million, federal civilian customers USD 725 million, international governments USD 706 million and commercial and infrastructure customers USD 2,018 million, and commercial and infrastructure clients were 94.3% of Sustainable Technology Solutions revenue. Backlog is 38% executable within one year, and nearly all contracts allow customers to terminate for convenience, so visibility is real but not binding.
Basis: calculation F17; calculation F19; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46

Pricing power is limited by the contract form rather than by market position. In Mission Technology Solutions the price is allowable cost plus fee under federal rules, procurement practice sometimes emphasises price over technical merit, and many contracts are recompeted, so margin comes from mix and execution. In Sustainable Technology Solutions the company says its technology portfolio enhances margins and attributes the fall in operating income to licensing mix, so a shift toward engineering and professional services is the likely reason revenue rose 11.1% while operating income fell 8%. The split of revenue between licensing and services is not printed, so pricing power on licences is not testable.

Customer concentration is high at group level. U.S. government customers were 57% and U.K. government customers 9% of fiscal 2025 revenue with no other customer above 10%, while Sustainable Technology Solutions drew 35.1% of its revenue from the Middle East against 26.4% a year earlier, a regional concentration tied to energy investment. Pass-through is strong where cost-reimbursable (38.2% of revenue) and weak where fixed-price (31.9%), and 53% of backlog is fixed-price or private finance initiative work that is predominantly fixed price. Revenue is therefore predictable and partly recurring in government work, cyclical and region-exposed in the technology business, and not structurally declining.

### Cost structure and margin resilience

Cost of revenues is 85.5% of revenue and is made up of project costs whose labour and materials split is not printed, so operating leverage is low on the evidence available: gross margin was 14.5% against 14.6% a year earlier while selling, general and administrative costs fell to 7.0% of revenue from 7.3%, helped by a favourable closeout in the first quarter whose amount is not stated. Operating margin fell to 9.1% from 9.9% because spin-off costs and other charges rose by USD 66 million, which also drove a 22% rise in the corporate operating loss, while group gross profit was flat.
Basis: calculation F3; calculation F21; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44

Margins can be defended under volume pressure where costs are reimbursable, since allowable costs and a fee are recovered, but not under cost inflation on fixed-price work, where the company says technical problems, schedule delays, workforce issues, material availability and inflation can raise costs to complete and reduce profit. Group margin stability is masked by segment movement: Mission Technology Solutions gross margin rose to 13.9% from 12.4% while Sustainable Technology Solutions fell to 15.6% from 19.2%. After separation both companies must replicate shared corporate functions, and the annual report warns that costs now treated as variable may become fixed and that stranded costs may arise, an exposure the allocation of corporate costs of USD 71 million in Adjusted EBITDA will settle.

Capital intensity is low and flexible: capital spending of USD 36 million is 0.61% of revenue and well below depreciation and amortisation of USD 126 million, operating lease payments were USD 61 million, and the company paid USD 40 million of spin-off transaction costs in cash. Free cash flow converted 44.4% of reported EBITDA in nine months against 54.4% in fiscal 2025 and 67.3% a year earlier, with equity earnings that arrive as distributions rather than consolidated cash lowering conversion: only 66.5% of equity earnings was declared as distributions in the period.

### Competitive forces

Competitive rivalry is intense in federal services: contracts are awarded competitively, often under multiple-award vehicles, and recompetes let rivals take share, with larger competitors holding more resources, so margin on new awards can be pressed. Barriers to entry are real but not decisive: cleared staff, facility clearances and past performance protect incumbency, yet award protests can delay revenue and cash. The credit effect is limited share loss at the margin rather than a sudden step-down.

Substitutes matter in two places: government agencies can insource work, as the NASA insourcing debooking shows and as the company says it competes with the government's own capabilities, and rapid technology change could erode the edge of licensed processes. Buyer power is high because the U.S. government is 57% of revenue, can modify or terminate contracts for convenience and reviews costs for allowability, and commercial energy customers defer projects when commodity prices move. Supplier power is modest, since equipment and materials come from a variety of global sources, but letters of credit and surety capacity beyond the revolver are at providers' discretion, which makes banks the supplier that matters to awards.
### Political, regulatory and economic factors

Political and regulatory factors are material to credit. The fiscal 2027 federal budget is not enacted, the continuing resolution lapses on 2026-12-11, an April 2026 executive order directs reviews of private-sector contracts, federal staff reductions may delay awards, and procurement reform may raise competition and compliance burdens; against this, defence appropriations of USD 839 billion for fiscal 2026 and NATO and Australian spending commitments support demand. For creditors the effect is timing risk to Mission Technology Solutions awards and cash, not a demonstrated loss of revenue.

Economic factors matter through commodity prices, tariffs and currency. Customer capital spending in oil, gas and chemicals responds to commodity prices, Sustainable Technology Solutions revenue is concentrated in the Middle East, and currency exposure on the balance sheet is hedged with forwards of USD 279 million of notional, all of 33 days or less. Social and technological factors are not primary credit drivers on the filings read.

### Credit-translated SWOT

Strengths that support credit are low capital intensity, a cost-reimbursable core, covered near-term maturities, a visible order book and the absence of a sponsor. Weaknesses that constrain credit are the unquantified separation financing, earnings that lean on LNG estimate changes and joint venture equity earnings, margin dilution at the business that stays, and fixed-price and joint venture guarantee exposure.
Basis: calculation F8; calculation F13; calculation F14; calculation F19; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Opportunities that could improve credit are a distribution large enough to hold leverage at about the current level, a record Sustainable Technology Solutions backlog converting to revenue, a re-awarded USD 8 billion ceiling Antarctic contract in Mission Technology Solutions that is not yet in backlog and supports the spun business's financing capacity, and a settlement with the U.S. Transportation Command that converted a termination for default to one for convenience. Threats that could weaken credit are a funding lapse, NASA and European command reductions, fade of LNG estimate benefits, stranded costs and higher interest after swaps end.

### Financial profile and credit quality

Scale is adequate and breadth is moderate: trailing revenue of USD 7,820 million comes from two segments, U.S. and U.K. government customers are 66% of fiscal 2025 revenue, and the business that stays is smaller, less diversified and more exposed to the Middle East. Cost and capex flexibility is good because capital spending is 0.61% of revenue and 38.2% of revenue is cost-reimbursable. Margin stability is average at group level, with gross margin at 14.5% against 14.6%, and weaker in the business that stays, where gross margin fell to 15.6% from 19.2%. Free cash flow is lower and more discretionary than a year ago, at USD 295 million against USD 482 million. The ability to refinance cannot be tested against ratings or prices because none are supplied; the only market evidence is fair values at 97.2% of principal for the Senior Notes and 100.2% for Term Loan B. Liquidity is adequate at 1.89x current maturities, and financial policy is restrained but undocumented. The trend is flat leverage on lower cash generation, and the missing data that matter are the separation financing, covenant ratios and definitions, and corporate cost allocation.

### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

In the next 12 to 24 months the near-term outlook is set by fiscal 2026 guidance for the whole group: revenue of USD 7,900 million to USD 8,360 million, Adjusted EBITDA of USD 980 million to USD 1,040 million and adjusted operating cash flow of USD 560 million to USD 600 million, which imply USD 203 million to USD 263 million of fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA against USD 268 million in the third quarter, so guidance leaves room for a fourth-quarter step-down or is cautious. Management says it will issue standalone outlooks with the spin-off, and separate investor days for KBR and Trinzic are scheduled for 2026-11-11 and 2026-11-12, after the as-of date, so nothing from them is used. Tailwinds are the record Sustainable Technology Solutions backlog, new awards in ammonia and offshore engineering, a re-awarded Antarctic support contract in Mission Technology Solutions that is not yet in backlog, and the lenders' consent to the reorganisation; headwinds are the funding lapse risk, NASA insourcing, the Mission Technology Solutions book-to-bill of 0.6x, and swap expiry.

Basis: calculation F20; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_q326kbr-exhibit991x10022026.htm.jsonl, pages 3–6; EX-99.1_2026-07-30_q226kbr-exhibit991x07032026.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 37

Over three to five years defence budgets and allied commitments support Mission Technology Solutions demand, and energy security and fertiliser capacity support the technology business, but the benefit goes to two separate companies. Sector tailwinds are NATO's 5% of GDP commitment by 2035, Australia's 3.00% of GDP by 2033 and the proposed fiscal 2027 defence budget; company-specific tailwinds are technology backlog and joint venture earnings. Headwinds are procurement reform, price-led awards, commodity-price sensitivity of energy customers and the Middle East concentration of the business that stays.
Basis: calculation F17; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, pages 36–38; 10-K_2026-01-02_kbr-20260102.htm.jsonl, page 56; 10-K_2026-01-02_kbr-20260102.htm.jsonl, page 60
### Qualitative downside scenario

The scenario begins with the separation financing, because it is the one event that moves leverage without any change in operations. If the spun business's financing yields a distribution of only 1.0x its annualised Adjusted EBITDA, USD 588 million, net debt after the distribution would be USD 1,514 million against annualised Adjusted EBITDA of USD 448 million for the business that stays, or 3.38x. At the same time a lapse in funding after 2026-12-11 could delay Mission Technology Solutions awards, favourable LNG estimate changes could stop, and the fourth quarter could land below the USD 203 million Adjusted EBITDA implied by the guidance floor.
Basis: calculation F8; calculation F13; calculation F20; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, page 52

The first operational break would be a stall in Sustainable Technology Solutions earnings, already down 6.5% without the new add-back, together with weaker cash conversion if customer advances unwind below the USD 331 million of fiscal 2025. The financial transmission is higher leverage on lower EBITDA, a step-up in interest as swaps with USD 955 million of notional end by January 2027, and a refinancing of Term Loan A-2 in August 2027 negotiated at a higher leverage. Liquidity would hold, since cash and undrawn revolver of USD 1,046 million cover USD 554 million of current maturities 1.89x, so the pressure is on leverage, pricing and covenant room rather than on liquidity distress. Management levers are USD 63 million of dividends, USD 29 million of repurchases, USD 189 million of discretionary investments and USD 36 million of capital spending. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through 2027 but not to preserve the current 2.07x.
Basis: calculation F5; calculation F8; calculation F10; calculation F12; calculation F14; calculation F16; 10-Q_2026-10-02_kbr-20261002.htm.jsonl, pages 28–29

The primary downside path is a small separation distribution that leaves most existing debt on the business that earns 43.2% of Adjusted EBITDA, followed by a government funding delay and a fade in LNG estimate benefits, with the first observable signs being the Form 10 financing terms, the fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA against USD 203 million and the treatment of Term Loan A-2.
Basis: calculation F7; calculation F8; calculation F13; calculation F20
### Overall credit view

Overall, KBR presents an adequate business profile supported by low capital intensity, a cost-reimbursable government core, covered near-term maturities and a visible order book, but credit quality is constrained by an unquantified separation financing that will move debt onto a business holding 43.2% of nine-month Adjusted EBITDA, by earnings quality that leans on LNG estimate changes and joint venture equity earnings, and by margin dilution at the business that stays. Cash-flow durability appears adequate due to low capital spending, cost pass-through and USD 515 million of fiscal 2025 free cash flow, but it is lower and more discretionary in 2026. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the size of the separation distribution, the extension of Term Loan A-2, the fate of the swaps and market access that no rating or price evidences. The primary downside path is a small distribution followed by a funding delay and a fade in LNG benefits. Further analysis would require the Form 10 financing and debt allocation, the covenant definitions and ratios, corporate cost allocation, and the executed credit agreement. Top risk: remaining-group leverage after separation.
Basis: calculation F1; calculation F7; calculation F8; calculation F9; calculation F13; Source readiness (CP-0); Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
